text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.3% today, continuing a sharp two-week decline that's now at nearly 7%. The drop reflects conflicting pressures on oil markets: while a potential U.S.-Iran diplomatic deal and the possibility of reopening the Strait of Hormuz are raising hopes for improved supply (which would lower prices), the Trump administration is simultaneously examining a diesel export ban that could restrict U.S. refining output. For an oil major like ConocoPhillips, lower crude prices (US oil at $107/barrel today) directly hurt profitability, even as supply uncertainty creates confusion about where energy prices head next.

The broader uncertainty is weighing on the sector. Analysts openly admit they don't know which way oil will break amid shifting geopolitical signals—Iran diplomacy potentially easing supply fears, but also talk of trade restrictions and energy embargoes that could fragment markets. This murky outlook, combined with crude prices sliding from the $141 level two weeks ago, has left investors cautious on energy stocks.
